title: Building Digital Banking Foundations: Delivering End-to-End FinTech Solutions with Enterprise-Grade Reliability
venue: International Journal of Research and Applied Innovations (IJRAI)
tldr: Presents a full-stack FinTech development initiative for community banks, demonstrating significant improvements in operational reliability, engineering velocity, and system stability through an Agile, CI/CD-driven enterprise architecture.
problem_and_motivation: Community banks face the challenge of providing modern digital banking functionalities with limited budgets on aging infrastructures, while maintaining high security and reliability. There is a need for a sustainable, enterprise-grade digital core that balances innovation with operational stability.
approach: Adopted a Scrum-based Agile SDLC with 2-week sprints and CI/CD automation using Jenkins.
Developed modular, RESTful microservices with Java and Spring for backend, and a component-based Angular frontend.
Used SQL Server for data management and deployed on AWS cloud services.
Implemented quality engineering with multi-layered testing including unit, integration, and performance testing.
Maintained a dual focus on new feature development and stabilization of existing production systems.
JIRA was used for backlog management, and Confluence for architectural documentation.
POCs were conducted for workflow engines and caching strategies to de-risk architectural decisions.
Used centralised logging and proactive monitoring to enhance operational visibility.
findings: num: Monthly production incidents reduced by 39.6% (from 48 to 29).
num: Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR) decreased by 47.2% (from 18 to 9.5 hours).
num: Sprint velocity improved by 76% (from an 85-112 baseline to 150 story points).
num: High-severity defects per quarter reduced by 47.6% (from 21 to 11).
num: System uptime availability increased from 98.1% to 99.4%.
Reduced carry-over tasks per sprint from 7 to 2.
The project delivered new end-to-end modules like customer onboarding and automated approvals.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a detailed case study on the implementation of an enterprise-grade digital banking platform for community banks. It provides empirical evidence on how a combination of modern engineering practices, such as Agile SDLC, CI/CD, and microservices architecture, can significantly improve operational stability and team productivity. The paper offers a practical benchmark by quantifying improvements in key metrics like production incidents, MTTR, and sprint velocity.
directly_justifies: A disciplined Agile and DevOps approach significantly improves production stability.
Automated testing and CI/CD pipelines reduce high-severity defects.
Enterprise-grade FinTech solutions are achievable for community banks.
System uptime can be improved through proactive monitoring and engineering quality.
limits: The paper does not address the integration of AI or machine learning for predictive tasks.
No analysis of user-specific budgeting or spending patterns is provided.
The architecture is not designed for an offline-first experience.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan of all topic domains in the taxonomy was performed. The paper was flagged as relevant primarily for domain 12.A (Evaluation Frameworks) due to its extensive quantitative results, and for 10.A (Data Privacy and Security) because security is a fundamental design principle. Domains such as 6.A (Predictive Modeling) and 8.A (Anomaly Detection) were marked as contextual, as they are identified only as future work. Domains like 1.A (Filipino Young Professionals) and 7.A (Budgeting Strategies) were rejected as the paper is an international, enterprise-level case study, not focused on individual behavior. The overall coverage is centered on platform engineering and operational reliability, not personal finance management features.

limitations: The study is a case study of a specific implementation, limiting generalizability. [unacknowledged]
The paper does not include a formal comparison with alternative technological approaches. [unacknowledged]
